themes.compare_row: Competence before reliance; order of learning; take-the-tool-away test
themes.statement: People must build their own competence before relying on AI, and whether they can still do the work without the tool must be tested.
themes.details: order of learning; take-the-tool-away / withdrawal tests; capability vs competence

themes.compare_row: Change the situation, don't warn individuals; name who acts
themes.statement: Change situations, defaults and incentives rather than relying on warnings, labels or individual vigilance.
themes.details: each rule names who acts / one owner per rule; disclosure alone does not change conduct

themes.compare_row: Monoculture / smoothness is the headline risk; show named disagreement
themes.statement: A central new risk is monoculture: a few models or one smooth answer become the default route to knowledge, so answers should show where experts disagree rather than a single consensus.
themes.details: correlated errors; homogenisation; show named disagreement; no answers from nowhere

themes.compare_row: Count independent sources, not repetitions
themes.statement: Corroboration must count independent sources, not repetitions of the same source (including many AI outputs drawing on the same data).
themes.details: repetition raises belief; show who seeded a claim

themes.compare_row: Cite by default; link out; correction status travels in answers
themes.statement: AI answers should cite or link to their sources by default and send readers to them.
themes.details: correction and retraction status travels with what is cited; 'cited' means the passage supports the claim

themes.compare_row: Behavioral audits outside the vendor; shared versioned battery; no generation more biased; keep retired models
themes.statement: AI systems must be audited on their behavior by parties independent of the vendor.
themes.details: shared versioned test battery; each generation no more biased than the last; keep retired models; nobody grades their own work

themes.compare_row: Accountable owner + mandatory liability insurance, premiums disclosed
themes.statement: Every deployed AI system has a named accountable owner who bears liability for it.
themes.details: mandatory liability insurance; premiums disclosed

themes.compare_row: Stop counting papers; publishers' correction duties; DORA with teeth
themes.statement: Stop using publication counts, rankings and journal metrics to evaluate researchers and institutions.
themes.details: DORA with teeth; publishers must issue and deposit corrections and retractions promptly; correction should earn reputation

themes.compare_row: Pay coarsely to communities, never per item; per-retrieval pay is gamed
themes.statement: Money for the knowledge commons should flow coarsely to communities and institutions (pools, funds, dues), not as per-item or per-retrieval payments.
themes.details: per-item pay gets gamed; pay for the practice, never the item

themes.compare_row: Event-level telemetry with audit rights; two witnesses; canaries
themes.statement: AI systems must log what they retrieved and used, and independent parties must have the right to audit those logs.
themes.details: event-level telemetry; two witnesses; canary documents; open trace standard

themes.compare_row: Antitrust safe harbour for producers bargaining as a bloc
themes.statement: Knowledge producers should be able to bargain collectively with AI firms as a bloc, including through an antitrust safe harbour.
themes.details: coalition bargaining; the strong refuse to settle alone

themes.compare_row: Commons-rent tax / levy / owed dues as backstop
themes.statement: A levy, tax or mandatory dues on AI firms should fund the knowledge commons, at least as a backstop if voluntary deals fail.
themes.details: commons-rent tax; owed dues

themes.compare_row: Separate controls for training vs grounding
themes.statement: Permissions for using content to train models should be separate from permissions for retrieving it to ground answers.

themes.compare_row: "Open to read is not open to train" as majority text
themes.statement: Being openly readable does not make a work open to AI training: training use requires the rights holders' or creators' consent (opt-in), at least for some classes of work.
themes.details: opt-in for in-copyright books; renewed consent

themes.compare_row: Honour Wikipedia's chosen licence; crawlers self-identify; reusers fund infrastructure
themes.statement: AI reusers must honor the licenses chosen by open knowledge projects such as Wikipedia, and heavy reusers should fund the infrastructure they draw on.
themes.details: attribution / share-alike; crawlers self-identify

themes.compare_row: Refusal is fundable
themes.statement: A community's refusal to have its knowledge taken or used is legitimate, binding and should be funded, not penalized.

themes.compare_row: Forkable infrastructure: CC0, open source, patent non-assertion, living will, non-US copy
themes.statement: Knowledge infrastructure must be forkable and allow exit: open data and open source, with copies outside any one jurisdiction or company.
themes.details: CC0; patent non-assertion; living will; non-US mirror; open means you can leave

themes.compare_row: Whoever profits from a count doesn't set it
themes.statement: Whoever profits from a count or metric must not set or control it.

themes.compare_row: Southern / diamond journals govern with binding say and funded seats
themes.statement: Global South institutions, diamond open-access journals and similar communities must hold binding governance power, with funded seats, in the bodies and funds being created.
themes.details: regional co-governance; CARE/OCAP

themes.compare_row: Identify agents and campaigns, never readers; anonymity stays
themes.statement: Automated agents and coordinated campaigns should be identified, but human readers should not be; anonymity is preserved.

themes.compare_row: Failure and negative results as first-class data
themes.statement: Failures, errors, null and negative results are first-class data that must be published and preserved.
themes.details: failure classes published; replication

themes.compare_row: Checkers as a paid body with a charter / Ulysses pact for every body
themes.statement: The bodies that check (auditors, fact-checkers, the new funds and institutions) must be paid and bound in advance by a public charter that answers who guards the guards.
themes.details: Ulysses pact; watching line funded first; sunset / review terms

themes.compare_row: Human in the loop is not a safeguard; overreliance; explanations can worsen it
themes.statement: A human in the loop is not by itself a safeguard: people over-rely on AI and adopt its errors and biases.
themes.details: explanations can make it worse

themes.compare_row: Test every seat, human or machine, against a floor; novelty test
themes.statement: Any gatekeeper, human or machine (such as an AI reviewer), must pass a published performance test before it is trusted, including the ability to recognize novelty.
themes.details: agreement with experts at least as high as between two human reviewers

themes.compare_row: No AI stand-ins for children, grief, therapy
themes.statement: AI should not stand in for people in intimate roles such as companionship for children, grief or therapy.
themes.details: no first-person 'I' or simulated feeling

themes.compare_row: Global majority is more hopeful than this room
themes.statement: People in the global majority / Global South are more hopeful about AI than this room, and that hope should shape the agenda.

themes.compare_row: Environmental and moderator costs in the ledger
themes.statement: The environmental costs of AI and the human costs of moderation and data work belong in the ledger.

themes.compare_row: Apprenticeship and first jobs as a funded line item
themes.statement: Apprenticeships, entry-level jobs and the training of new experts and checkers must be funded, because AI erodes the path from novice to expert.
themes.details: fellowships; employers keep entry-level roles with mentors

themes.statement: The document names who was missing from the room and commits to including them in a future convening.

baseline_themes.statement: Most of the crisis predates AI: AI accelerates old failures, so remedies must distinguish what was already broken from what AI newly breaks.
AI systems should be described by what they actually do, neither as minds or oracles nor as mere autocomplete.
Evaluation and verification, not production, are now the scarce resource, so investment should shift from producing knowledge to checking it.
Credibility should rest on checkable process, track record and accountable people or communities, not on fluency, polish or credentials.
Provenance and attribution are infrastructure that must be built into knowledge systems and AI tools.
The human labor behind trustworthy knowledge (reviewing, editing, curating, checking) must be made visible and paid.
AI tools should be designed to strengthen human judgment and capability rather than replace it.
No single company, state or model should control the infrastructure of knowledge; concentrated control of it is a central risk that needs public options or governance.
Knowledge institutions and the knowledge commons are public goods that deserve public investment and independence from platforms and states.

baseline_themes_note: The no-corpus baseline's recurring principles (baseline-nocorpus/b1-b6), restated as core claims on 2026-09-27 before the real manifesto existed, excluding three already covered above (stop paying for volume = stop_counting_papers; plurality = monoculture; open but reciprocal commons = honour_licences). Scored on every document so the forward comparison does not only test sim 2's own themes.
